correctness.rationale: The package recursively generates tournament isomorphism representatives and canonicalizes exactly within out-degree blocks; the resulting counts \(1,1,2,4,12,56,456\) match the known independent catalogue. For each of the 532 classes it builds the full downward-closed out-neighborhood complex and exact integer boundary maps, checks the chain identities and computes homology invariant factors via Smith normal form in an integral kernel basis. I independently reran that exact census/SNF core: all 532 classes were processed and the torsion-witness list was empty. The finite quantifier is therefore exhaustive, not sampled.

value.rationale: The defining paper explicitly presents tournament-neighborhood torsion as an open phenomenon. Seven vertices is a natural next topological cutoff—large enough for the source's sphere construction to reach \(S^2\)—and the exact negative census raises the first possible torsion order to eight.
residual_risks: A later unindexed small-order computation may exist under directed-Hom terminology.

final_claim: Every tournament on at most seven vertices has torsion-free integral homology in its out-neighborhood complex; consequently any tournament neighborhood complex with integral torsion has at least eight vertices.
limitations: No statement is made for tournaments with at least eight vertices or for directed flag complexes.
